[Course index](../index.html)

These are reference examples, not an additional exercise. Replace the example object names with the objects in your notebook. Write commands in a chunk and run earlier chunks first.

| Task | Example |
|---|---|
| Store values | `scores <- c(27, 28, 30)` |
| Read a CSV | `mmse <- read.csv("data/mmse_baseline.csv")` |
| Inspect a table | `head(mmse)`; `dim(mmse)`; `names(mmse)`; `str(mmse)` |
| Select a column | `mmse$Age` |
| Select rows and columns | `mmse[1:5, c("Age", "MMSE")]` |
| Keep values above a threshold | `scores[scores > 25]` |
| Count values meeting a condition | `sum(scores > 25)`; check missing values first |
| Find positions | `which(scores > 25)` |
| Apply arithmetic to every value | `calibrated <- lengths_um * 0.98 - 0.15` |
| Wide to long for numeric group columns | `neurites_long <- stack(neurites)` |
| Count categories | `table(mmse$Group)` |
| Count missing values per column | `colSums(is.na(mmse))` |
| Count observed values | `sum(!is.na(mmse$MMSE))` |
| Keep scores from one group | `mmse$MMSE[mmse$Group == "Demented"]` |
| Centre and spread | `mean(scores)`; `median(scores)`; `sd(scores)`; `IQR(scores)` |
| Quartiles | `quantile(scores, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75))` |
| Range | `range(scores)` |
| Omit missing values in a summary | `mean(scores, na.rm = TRUE)` |
| Histogram | `hist(scores, xlab = "MMSE score (points)")` |
| Bar chart of category counts | `barplot(table(mmse$M.F), ylab = "Participants")` |
| Multiple panels | `par(mfrow = c(2, 2))`; reset with `par(mfrow = c(1, 1))` |
| Boxplot by group | `boxplot(MMSE ~ Group, data = mmse)` |
| Scatterplot | `plot(mmse$Age, mmse$MMSE)`; add meaningful axis labels |
| Normal Q–Q plot | `qqnorm(scores)` followed by `qqline(scores)` |
| Shapiro–Wilk | `shapiro.test(scores)` |
| Independent mean comparison | `result <- t.test(group1, group2)`; default is Welch |
| Independent rank-sum comparison | `result <- wilcox.test(group1, group2, exact = FALSE)` |
| Correlation with inference | `cor.test(x, y, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)` |
| Adjust a stated family | `p.adjust(p_values, method = "bonferroni")` |
| Read a result | `result` first, then for example `result$p.value` |
| Function help | `?t.test` in the Console |

`<-` assigns; `==` compares. Text and file paths need quotes; object names do not. Capitals matter. If your Console shows `+`, check for an unclosed bracket or quote; Esc cancels an unfinished command.

Before a test, state the question, observation unit, variables, and assumptions. After a test, report the relevant estimate, sample size, uncertainty where available, and limitations. A command running successfully does not establish that the analysis is appropriate.
